issues.title: Set up Python tooling and CI
issues.body:
Foundation for everything else. The triager lives in this repo from week 1, so set up tooling now rather than in week 2.

**Done when**
- `uv` project on Python 3.12+, with a `src/flight_recorder` package and an `afr` CLI entry point
- ruff (lint + format), pyright and pytest run in pre-commit and in GitHub Actions on every PR
- gitleaks runs in pre-commit and CI; a fake key in a test commit is blocked
- `.env.example` documents every setting
- A PR template with a `Closes #` line and a short checklist (tests, docs)

Estimate: ~1h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

issues.title: Provider-switchable LLM config
issues.body:
One setting chooses the provider for every agent and the judge, so runs, evals and costs can be compared across providers.

**Providers**
- Anthropic for local development and bulk runs. The key lives only in a local `.env`: never in GitHub secrets, CI or the deployed instance
- Gemini API free tier (personal Google AI Studio key) for CI and the provider comparison. GitHub Models, the original choice, was retired on 30 July 2026

**Done when**
- `AFR_LLM_MODEL` and `AFR_LLM_CHEAP_MODEL` accept either provider (e.g. `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5`, `google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) via LangChain `init_chat_model`
- Provider details, prices with sources, and Gemini free-tier limits noted in `docs/llm-providers.md`
- `pricing.yaml` holds per-model token prices for cost calculation (Gemini free tier recorded as $0; unknown models report `None`)
- A smoke test calls each provider with the same prompt, skipped when its key is missing

Estimate: ~0.5h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

issues.title: Issue fixtures for the triager
issues.body:
The triager triages this project's own issues: they're ours to commit, their labels and milestones are real ground truth, and the agent works on the repo it's recorded in.

**Done when**
- `scripts/export_issues.py` exports this repo's issues (title, body, labels, milestone, state, duplicate links) to `examples/issue_triager/fixtures/issues.json`, committed so CI and the quickstart need no GitHub access
- Ground truth per issue: area labels, `stretch` or not, milestone (week), duplicate-of (#3 is a real duplicate of #2)
- The agent never sees the target issue's own labels or milestone
- About 60 extra cases to make up for the small repo: paraphrased variants of real issues, and hand-written tricky ones (ambiguous area, cross-cutting, near-duplicates), marked as synthetic
- The export can be re-run as the issue list grows
- Nothing in the project writes to GitHub

Estimate: ~1h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

issues.title: Build the LangGraph issue triager
issues.body:
The demo agent whose runs the recorder captures. Keep it deliberately imperfect so it produces real failures to study.

**Done when**
- LangGraph state graph: read issue -> search similar issues -> pick area labels, `stretch` or not, milestone, possible duplicate or regression -> draft a triage comment
- Tools work only on the fixtures (dry-run); nothing writes to GitHub
- Human-in-the-loop interrupt before the "apply" step
- `uv run triager --issue <n>` runs end to end on both providers
- A flag injects tool failures (timeouts, bad data) for testing

Estimate: ~3h

## Design (agreed 6 Nov)

```
load_issue -> triage (LLM + tools, loops) -> validate --invalid--> retry triage once, then fail
                                                |
                                                v ok
                                      draft_comment (cheap model) -> human_review (interrupt) -> apply (dry-run, local file)
```

| Part | Decision |
|---|---|
| Agent loop | Only inside `triage`: the LLM decides when and what to search, possibly several times. Other steps are fixed |
| Tools | `search_issues(query)`: top 5 similar issues with labels, week, state. `get_issue(id)`: one issue in full. The target issue never appears in results |
| Search | Keyword (BM25) over real issues only, for now. Embeddings come with #11; misses on reworded duplicates are expected, recordable failures |
| Input | `case.agent_input()` only: title and body, never the target's labels or milestone |
| Decision | Structured output with the same shape as `GroundTruth` plus `confidence` and `rationale`, so grading is a direct comparison |
| Validate | Code check: known areas, week 1-5 or none, linked ids exist, stretch needs a week. Retry once, then fail |
| Duplicates | Suggested only, worded as a suggestion. Closing a real issue by mistake is worse than missing a duplicate |
| Failures | Natural (plain prompt, no tuning, optional cheap model) and injected (`--inject timeout,bad-data,empty,noise --rate`) |
| Human review | Interactive y/n; `--yes` auto-approves for batch runs (#13) |
| Output | Decision + comment written to `runs/` (git-ignored) as the dry-run "apply" |

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

issues.title: Trace schema, migrations and local Postgres
issues.body:
Canonical store for every run, modelled on the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.

**Done when**

- SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migrations for `runs`, `spans` (parent/child tree, kind, model, tokens, cost, status, input/output JSONB, raw attributes), `embeddings`, `labels` and `eval_results`
- `docs/schema.md` explains the model and how OTel / OpenInference attributes map onto it
- Tests run against a real Postgres (service container in CI)

Estimate: ~1.5h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

FastAPI ingest for OpenTelemetry traces, so any OTel-instrumented agent can be recorded.

**Done when**

- Spans map to runs/spans for both OTel GenAI (`gen_ai.*`) and OpenInference attributes; tokens and cost are filled in

Estimate: ~2.5h

issues.title: Claude Code hook capture
issues.body:
Record Claude Code sessions as runs with tool-call spans.

**Done when**
- `afr hook` reads hook JSON from stdin and posts it to `POST /v1/claude-code/events` for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStop, Stop and SessionEnd
- On Stop / SessionEnd, token usage is read from the session transcript
- The hook fails open and fast: if the API is down, Claude Code is never blocked or slowed
- Installed only through a project-level `.claude/settings.json`; docs warn against a user-level install on work machines
- A Claude Code session in this repo shows up as a run with its tool calls

Estimate: ~1.5h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md

issues.title: Redaction guardrail at ingest
issues.body:
Nothing sensitive is ever stored. The first guardrail, and a good README and interview story.

**Done when**
- Redacts API keys and tokens (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, AWS, GCP, generic high-entropy strings), private keys, connection strings, emails and phone numbers
- Runs on every ingest path before any write; the hook also does a first pass client-side
- Stores redaction counts per span, never the original values
- Tests cover each pattern, and a planted canary secret never reaches the database

Estimate: ~1h

Plan: https://github.com/sonicjoy/agent-flight-recorder/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md
